chapter_title: The Human is less than all the Things of the Universe, and he is rebellious beyond them all.
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by hagiographic travel narrative and polemical/theodicy application (humanity’s blasphemy; denying that demons come from God). The oldest cosmological substrate appears only in brief embedded fragments: (a) Jesus’ non-anthropocentric, cosmic ‘task’ in the great universe and his revelation to Adam and Eve; (b) compressed cosmology items (aeons/Greatness, Light vs Darkness, descent to the province of death) preserved inside later catechetical list-format; and (c) a short cosmological description of the Cross of Light embedded in a moral injunction. No paragraph is “pure core” without later framing; the core survives mostly as extractable fragments inside later catechesis.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic itinerary scene with the title “apostle” and narrative staging; functions as editorial container, not cosmological exposition.

Continues the illustrative story (measurement comparison) in a narrated setting; present-time anchor (“today”) and anecdotal rhetoric. The phrase “five wo[r]ds of the f]lesh” may echo an older scheme, but it is too embedded in the later exemplum to extract securely.
Application/theodicy rhetoric contrasting mute creation with human blasphemy; not systematic cosmos→cosmos mapping but moralizing/polemical discourse directed at contemporary belief about evil.
Explicit polemic against attributing rulers/demons to God; maps doctrine onto contemporary accusations (“they say…”), crossing from being-description to argumentative application.
Classic dialogue prompt (“one of his disciples… Tell us, our master”)—editorial Q&A apparatus.
NT-vector material: Jesus as “son of the Living God,” crucifixion, cross, persecution—dependent on Christian passion tradition rather than internal cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: Jesus did not come and s[a]ve the world because of mankind alone, but [ ... he] came and revealed on earth [ ... ] was strong outside in [ ... ] And [whe]n he had finished doing his [t]ask outside [i]n the great u[ni]verse, he came [ ... he wen]t further with Adam and Eve and revealed [to them].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (“[The ap]ostle [says] to him:”) as hagiographic frame. Removed the institutional/catechetical extension (“Even so, he sent the apostles… generation by generation… revealed… five great thin[gs]”) because it shifts from cosmological role to church/apostolic transmission scheme.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core fragment is cosmological and non-institutional (Jesus’ ‘task’ in the great universe; revelation to primordial humans). The surrounding apostolic-lineage and list-introduction is later catechetical framing.

paragraphs.core_text: they belong to the race of Ligh[t].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed list label and didactic narration (“[Firs]t: He told them that…”) as catechetical framing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Old doctrinal identity formula (“race of Light”) preserved as a bullet-point inside a later ‘five things’ catechetical list.

paragraphs.core_text: the aeons [of the greatness], how they occur; and [the manner of] the Darkness, how it t[o]o exists.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed list label and pedagogic verbs (“[Se]cond: He unveiled to them about… and he taught them about…”) as later catechetical framing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos-internal ontological topics (aeons/Greatness; Darkness’ mode of existence) indicate substrate teaching, but they enter here via a later list format about what was ‘revealed to them’.

paragraphs.core_text: the [L]ight great-[ness], how it has been active against the pow[er of] Darkness and conquered it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed list label and pedagogic preface (“[The th]ird time: He proclaimed to them about…”) as catechetical framing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-mechanical Light vs Darkness conquest belongs to the cosmological substrate, but is preserved in an enumerated catechism-style item.

paragraphs.core_text: he came to the province of death [ ... ... ] that is flesh, until he should find profit and bring them from the gate of the underworld below, for [they had] been swa[ll]owed into it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed list label and pedagogic wrapper (“Fourth: He taught them that…”) as catechetical framing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological-soteriological mechanics (descent to the ‘province of death’/flesh; extraction from underworld gate) read as older mythic teaching embedded in later instructional enumeration.

paragraphs.core_text: the rebels shall be bound in a great fetter, they who shall [r]ebel against the g[o]od and against the righteousness
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed list label and audience/pedagogic wrapper (“Fifth: He explained to us that…”) as catechetical framing. Removed the institutional tag “t[hat] is proclaimed by the apostle” as later community authority-marking.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological binding motif can belong to core mechanics, but the paragraph in situ is a catechetical ‘fifth item’ and is explicitly tied to apostolic proclamation (late authority anchor).
Dialogue attribution (“Once [again] the apostle speaks”) plus catechetical announcement about ‘the faithful’ indicates later instructional framing, not substrate exposition.
Catechetical identity marking of ‘the faithful’ in list format; community-facing instruction rather than impersonal cosmological architecture.
Institutional authority marker (“the [a]postle who has been manifested”) and community faith confession; not cosmos→cosmos mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: the Cross of Light, which g[rie]ves in the totality, being present in what is visible and what is not vis[ib]le.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ethical/instructional wrapper (“The third: They a[ct] with restraint and charity to…”) as pastoral application; retained the cosmological description of the Cross of Light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The imperative ethical layer (‘restraint and charity’) is later pastoral application, but the Cross of Light as a cosmic, all-pervasive structure (‘visible and not visible’) is a substrate cosmological datum.
